title: Supplier management (add-on)
description: Supplier approval, reviews, a library of supplier requirements with the rules for who they apply to, and a check per supplier and requirement kept in step for you, on the shared Suppliers register of the Core registers. Supplier documents go in Documents and policies, supplier risks in the Risk register and supplier problems in Nonconformities and CAPA. Installs the Core registers first.

sheets.name: Supplier reviews
sheets.description: Periodic reviews of a supplier with the result and what to follow up.

sheets.name: Supplier requirements
sheets.description: The master list of what suppliers are held to, with the rules for which suppliers each applies to. The sync adds a check per supplier and requirement.

fields.name: Applies to
fields.description: Every supplier, by category and criticality, suppliers that process personal data (the Art. 28 set) or only when added by hand.

fields.name: Applies to categories
fields.description: Empty: every category. Matched to the supplier’s category by option or by name.

fields.name: Applies from criticality
fields.description: The lowest criticality it applies to. Empty: every criticality.

fields.name: Framework requirements
fields.description: The ISO/IEC 27001, ISO 9001 or GDPR requirements this meets, where you have adopted them.

items.name: Signed contract with information security terms

values.guidance: The contract says how the supplier protects our information, who may access it and that we may check it.
The supplier and the people who work for us have signed a confidentiality agreement before they see our information.
A signed agreement sets out what the supplier does with personal data on our behalf, only on our instructions.
We have the list of sub-processors, approved it and are told before a new one is added.

items.name: Transfer mechanism for data outside the EEA

values.guidance: Where personal data leaves the EEA, the mechanism is named: adequacy, standard contractual clauses or binding corporate rules.
The supplier tells us about a security incident that affects us within 24 hours.
We may audit the supplier, or receive an independent report in its place, at least once a year.

items.name: Data returned or deleted at exit

values.guidance: When the contract ends, the supplier returns or deletes our data and confirms it in writing.

items.name: Valid ISO/IEC 27001 certificate or SOC 2 report

values.guidance: A current certificate or report covers the service we buy. Record when it expires.

items.name: Business continuity plan for the service

values.guidance: The supplier has a tested plan to keep the service running, or restore it, after a disruption.
The supplier holds liability insurance that fits the work. Record when the policy ends.
The supplier sends a current certificate of its quality management system each year.
We measure on-time and right-first-time delivery and review it with the supplier.

sheets.name: Supplier requirement checks
sheets.description: One check per supplier and requirement: the status, the evidence and when it expires. Added and flagged by the sync; never deleted. Access follows the supplier register (same folder).

rules.message: Say why it does not apply and who approved it before marking it Not applicable.

fields.name: Source
fields.description: Rule and Art. 28 checks are kept in step by the sync; checks added by hand are never flagged.

fields.name: Wording when checked
fields.description: The requirement as it read when the check was answered. Set by an automation.

fields.name: Version when checked
fields.description: The library version when the check was answered. Set by an automation.

fields.name: Sync note
fields.description: Why the sync flagged or reopened the check.

automations.name: Review due in 14 days → ask the owner for an update

actions.message: {id} {name} is due for review on {next_review}. Please plan it.

automations.name: Supplier added → sync its requirement checks
automations.description: Cascade: a new supplier gets one check for every library requirement that applies to its category, criticality and personal data, so nobody has to work out which requirements apply by hand. The owner is told when the new checks lower the share met.

automations.name: Category changed → sync the requirement checks
Criticality changed → sync the requirement checks
Processes personal data changed → sync the requirement checks
Extra requirements changed → sync the requirement checks
Sync requirements button → sync the requirement checks
Supplier review 14 days late → tell the owner and top management
automations.description: Escalation ladder: the owner is asked 14 days before the review date. A supplier still not reviewed 14 days after it goes to top management with the owner, because an unreviewed supplier is a gap in supplier control.

actions.message: {id} {name} was due for review on {next_review} and has not been reviewed.

values.cause: One provider hosts every customer system
values.consequence: Customers cannot use the service; credits and lost trust

layout.title: Report a supplier problem
layout.description: A late or wrong delivery, a service that went down, a security or data problem at a supplier, or a supplier not doing what the contract says.
layout.nameLabel: What went wrong, in one line

settings.confirmation: Thank you. The supplier owner has your report.

automations.name: Supplier problem reported → tell the owner of the nonconformity

actions.message: Supplier problem reported: {id} {name}. Contain it and decide whether the supplier needs a review.

automations.name: Review failed → tell the supplier owner

actions.message: {name} of {supplier} failed. Decide what happens next.

automations.name: Requirement added → add its checks to the suppliers it applies to
automations.description: Cascade across sheets: a requirement added to the library is checked at every supplier it applies to (in batches of 200), so a new rule reaches the whole supplier base at once.

automations.name: Applies to changed → re-sync the suppliers
Applies to categories changed → re-sync the suppliers
Applies from criticality changed → re-sync the suppliers
Guidance changed → raise the version
Check answered → record who, when and the wording it was checked against
Check not met → tell the supplier owner

actions.message: {supplier} does not meet "{name}" ({id}). Decide what happens next.

automations.name: Evidence expires in 30 days → tell the supplier owner

actions.message: Evidence for "{name}" ({id}) at {supplier} expires on {evidence_expiry}. Ask for new evidence.

automations.name: Review failed → raise a nonconformity and link it
automations.description: Cross-sheet cascade: a failed supplier review raises a linked item in Nonconformities and CAPA (source Supplier), where the containment, root cause and corrective actions are tracked until it can close with a verified effect.

automations.name: Review passed → move the supplier’s next review a year on
automations.description: Recurring review cycle: when a review passes, with or without conditions, the supplier’s next review date moves to a year from now, so every supplier comes up for review again without anyone setting the date.

setup.title: Supplier management setup
setup.description: Four steps to a supplier base you can show an auditor. Each step’s progress comes from your sheets.

steps.title: List your suppliers
steps.body: Add the suppliers you depend on, each with an owner, a category and a criticality. Their requirement checks are added for you.

steps.title: Decide what you require
steps.body: Read the supplier requirements, change the guidance to fit you and say which suppliers each applies to.

steps.title: Check each supplier
steps.body: Answer every check with the evidence and when it expires. Not applicable needs a reason and who approved it.

steps.title: Approve your suppliers
steps.body: Submit each supplier for approval: its owner, then top management. Give someone the job title Top management so the approval has someone to ask.
